title: Palindrome Partitioning
description:
Split the string `s` into consecutive pieces so that **every piece reads the same forwards and backwards**. Return all such partitions.

Each partition is a list of substrings that concatenate back to `s`. The partitions may be returned in any order, but the pieces inside a partition must stay in their original order.

examples.explanation: "aab" itself is not a palindrome, so it cannot be a single piece.

constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters
hints: Choose where the first piece ends. If s[start:end] is a palindrome, recurse on the remainder.
Recurse with a `start` index; for each `end` > start, check the palindrome, push the piece, recurse from `end`, pop.
Palindrome checks are O(L) each; precomputing a 2-D `is_pal[i][j]` table in O(n^2) makes each check O(1), though for n <= 16 the direct check is fine.
approach:
**Key insight: a partition is determined by where each piece ends, so recurse on the start index and only extend with pieces that are palindromes.** Non-palindromic prefixes are pruned immediately, which is what makes this backtracking rather than enumerating all 2^(n-1) cut sets.

**Algorithm.** `backtrack(start)`: if `start == n` record the path. Otherwise for each `end` in `[start, n)`, if `s[start..end]` is a palindrome, push it, recurse from `end + 1`, pop.

**Why it works.** Every valid partition corresponds to a unique sequence of palindrome end points, and every such sequence is visited exactly once. The palindrome test is the only pruning needed.

**Common mistakes:** off-by-one on the slice (`s[start:end+1]`); recomputing palindrome checks without noticing the O(n^2) DP table is available; returning references to `path`.

**Interview follow-ups:** Minimum number of cuts instead of all partitions? (Palindrome Partitioning II, O(n^2) DP.) Precompute `is_pal` with the expand-from-the-inside recurrence `is_pal[i][j] = s[i]==s[j] and is_pal[i+1][j-1]`? (yes, fill by increasing length.) Worst case? (a string of one repeated letter: every split is valid, 2^(n-1) partitions.)

complexity.space: O(n) recursion, plus O(n^2) if a palindrome table is used
